To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tree canopies act as magnifiers and reducers for the climatic regime and that the shifting nature of the canopy microclimate mosaic may explain the observed distribution of leaf mining insects.
(1) the canopy mosaic of microclimatic conditions experienced by leaf miners is highly heterogeneous and (2) the microclimatic mosaic is modulated by the regional climate and the canopy structure.
the mosaic of suitable microclimates for insect development is strongly dependent on the regional climate.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the canopy mosaic of suitable microhabitats for insects is highly dynamic.

climate change will not have the same impact on the population dynamics of a species, depending on the climatic conditions in the area where it lives, and the spatial distribution of the species within its habitat.
tree canopies are not simple microclimatic shelters for insects but rather a mosaic of favourable and unfavourable spots, depending on regional climate conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tree canopies are not just passive filters for the regional climatic signal.
the mosaic of microhabitats within the tree canopy is a major factor that determines the distribution and dynamics of leaf miner larvae.
the mosaic of microhabitats within tree canopies is not only determined by tree architecture but also by the regional climate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regional climatic context modulates the microclimate mosaic within tree canopies and, thus, may affect the distribution of organisms within canopies.
the impact of climatic change on organisms will be modulated by the regional climate and the canopy architecture.
the regional climatic context is a key determinant of the spatial heterogeneity of microclimates in tree canopies.
